i) there is a unique mechanism that satisfies individual rationality, consumer sovereignty and efficiency; ii) there are many mechanisms that satisfy individual rationality, budget balance and efficiency; and iii) the worst welfare loss of the Shapely value cost sharing formula mechanism is the least among all budget balanced mechanisms.

i) the Shapley cost sharing formula is the only cost sharing formula that leads to a strategyproof and budget balanced mechanism, and ii) this mechanism has a welfare loss that is minimal among the Shapley-based mechanisms.

the marginal contribution mechanism is unique among all efficient mechanisms, that there is a whole class of budget-balanced mechanisms (including the Shapley mechanism) each one immune to coalitional manipulations, and that MC is better than the Shapley-value mechanism in terms of budget imbalance and welfare loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how much do we have to pay for efficiency in the sharing of submodular costs?
the trade-off between budget balance and efficiency in the design of strategyproof cost-sharing mechanisms for submodular costs.
two fundamental problems: i) the tradeoff between efficiency and budget balance, and ii) the design of strategyproof cost sharing mechanisms.

the Shapley mechanism is a better choice than MC, in the sense that it is immune to manipulations and has the minimal welfare loss among all strategyproof and budgetbalanced mechanisms.

the Shapley-value-based mechanism is the best of the worst, in the sense that it minimizes the worst-case welfare loss, while maintaining budget balance and individual rationality, and it is the unique mechanism that does not require the assumption of consumer sovereignty to be strategyproof.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) there is a unique mechanism that is both strategyproof and efficient; and (2) there are many strategyproof mechanisms that are budget-balanced, and among them the Shapley mechanism minimizes welfare loss.

, when a network is not congested, MC is the unique mechanism that is both strategyproof and efficient, and the Shapley mechanism is the unique mechanism within the class of budget-balanced mechanisms that is strategyproof.
the Shapley cost sharing formula is the best compromise between efficiency and budget balance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of externalities, the Shapley-value mechanism is the best strategyproof mechanism in terms of welfare loss.
, for submodular costs, budget balance can be achieved at the expense of a significant welfare loss, and the latter is minimized by the Shapley mechanism.
budget balance and efficiency are not always compatible in the context of submodular cost sharing.
